common_name: Redruth Skimmia (Heavy-Berrying Female Evergreen Shade Shrub)

planting.note: Plant a male Skimmia pollinator such as 'Rubella' or 'Kew Green' within about 15 feet, since 'Redruth' is a vigorous female clone grown for its unusually large red berries.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, consistently moist, acidic to neutral soil in full to partial shade; 'Redruth' is a vigorous, larger-growing female Skimmia japonica selection with leathery, oval leaves noticeably bigger than the species. Tiny, fragrant white flowers open in spring and, once pollinated by a nearby male Skimmia, are followed by an especially heavy crop of larger-than-average glossy red berries that persist ornamentally into winter. Its more robust habit than many female cultivars suits it to woodland borders, shrub beds, and mass plantings where its fruit display can be appreciated from a distance. Mulch annually to conserve moisture and maintain soil acidity, water during dry spells, and limit pruning to light shaping after flowering since fruit forms on the previous year's growth.

common_name: Bronze Knight Skimmia (Bronze-Foliage Male Pollinator Evergreen Shrub)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, acidic soil in light to deep shade; 'Bronze Knight' is a male-flowering selection grown for its winter-bronzed foliage and as a fragrant pollinator, since it sets no berries.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, acidic soil in light to deep shade, where cool, shaded conditions bring out the best foliage color. 'Bronze Knight' is an open-habit male Skimmia japonica clone with lustrous, strongly pointed dark green leaves that take on an attractive bronze cast through the winter months. Dark red buds form in fall and open in spring into dense, fragrant clusters of small white flowers similar to 'Rubella'. As a male selection it produces no berries itself, but it is an effective pollinator for female Skimmia cultivars grown nearby for their fruit display. Water during dry spells, mulch to maintain even moisture and soil acidity, and prune only to remove dead or crossing wood.

common_name: Fragrant Mountain Sweet Box (Compact Himalayan Wonder Sarcococca)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in deep to partial shade; this Canadian patented selection is a companion introduction to 'Fragrant Valley' in the Himalayan Wonder series, with glossier, darker foliage than the species.

directions: Site in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in deep to partial shade. 'Fragrant Mountain' ('Sarsid2') is a naturally occurring mutation selected from Sarcococca hookeriana var. humilis seedlings by Sidhu & Sons Nursery in British Columbia and released alongside its sibling 'Fragrant Valley' as part of the patented Himalayan Wonder series. It forms a dense, mounded, multi-stemmed evergreen shrub that spreads slowly by suckering, with shiny, leathery leaves noticeably wider, glossier, and darker green than the species. Tiny but powerfully fragrant white flowers open in late winter and perfume the surrounding air with a sweet vanilla-honey scent, followed by berries that ripen from red to glossy black by summer and persist into the following winter. Once established it is drought tolerant in shade and essentially pest-free; water during extended dry spells and mulch to maintain even soil moisture.
